title: Quarto formats
summary: Make several outputs from one Quarto source. Create HTML, Word and PDF reports, slides, a dashboard with a table, and a small website.

steps.title: Setup: library(quarto)

runs.purpose: load quarto, which runs Quarto from R

steps.explain: Quarto comes with RStudio; the quarto package runs it from R code, as the Render button does from the toolbar. The documents in this lesson are already written: `29-report.qmd`, `29-slides.qmd`, `29-dashboard.qmd` and the `29-website` folder.

steps.title: One source, several formats: format:

runs.task: Open `29-report.qmd` from the Files pane, and read its YAML header.

runs.purpose: render the report with the Render button
runs.task: Render `29-report.qmd` with the Render button above it.

steps.explain:
The report's YAML header lists three formats under `format:`, each with its own options. For HTML, `toc: true` adds a table of contents built from the `##` headings, and `code-fold: true` hides each chunk's code behind a Code button, so readers see results first and code on request.

The Render button renders the first format listed, HTML, and the Viewer shows it: the contents at the side, and the chart's and table's code folded away.

steps.title: Word and PDF: quarto_render()

runs.purpose: render the same report as a Word document
runs.task: Render `29-report.qmd` as Word with `quarto_render()` and `output_format = "docx"`. (If the Background Jobs tab covers the Console, click the Console tab first.)

runs.purpose: render it as a PDF, through Typst
runs.task: Render it again with `output_format = "typst"`, which makes a PDF.

steps.explain:
The Render button ran Quarto in a Background Jobs tab, in front of the Console; the Console tab brings the Console back. `quarto_render()` renders a document from code, and `output_format` picks one of the formats in its header.

From the same text and code came `29-report.docx`, which anyone with Word can edit, and `29-report.pdf`, typeset by Typst, which comes with Quarto. Each format leaves out what it can't show: the Word and PDF versions have no folded code or contents sidebar.

Click a file in the Files pane, then Export or View, to look at it.

steps.title: Slides: revealjs
steps.explain:
With `format: revealjs`, each `##` heading starts a new slide, and the Viewer shows a slide show: click it, then press the arrow keys to move through.

The chunks and inline code run as in a report, so the numbers on the slides come from the data, and a bullet list is written as a Markdown list. To change the slides, change the text and render again.

steps.title: A dashboard: format: dashboard
steps.explain:
A dashboard lays out its chunks' output in cards instead of a page: each `##` heading makes a row, and each chunk a card, titled by its `#| title:` option.

The table is a `reactable()` htmlwidget: in the Viewer you can search it, sort it by clicking a column's name, and page through it, all in the browser, with no R running. Interactive widgets need HTML, so they work in reports, slides and dashboards, but not in Word or PDF.

steps.title: A website: a Quarto project

runs.purpose: render the website in the 29-website folder
runs.task: Render the whole `29-website` folder with `quarto_render()`, adding `as_job = FALSE` so that it renders in the Console.

steps.explain:
A folder with a `_quarto.yml` file is a Quarto project. `29-website/_quarto.yml` makes it a website and lists its pages in a navigation bar. Rendering the folder renders every page and writes the site to `29-website/_site`, ready to put on any web server.

In RStudio, `quarto_render()` renders a project as a background job unless told otherwise; `as_job = FALSE` renders it in the Console, where you can watch. The website lives in its own folder because a `_quarto.yml` at the top of this project would make every lesson's document part of the site.

Quarto projects can also be books, which number chapters and cross-references across files.
